did_you_know.text: Did you know? The threat to Judah came from a coalition of the Moabites, the Ammonites, and another group referred to in the verse as “the Ammonites”? They went to war against Jehoshaphat.
Did you know? In response to the military threat, Jehoshaphat did not rely only on war preparations: he sought the LORD and proclaimed a fast throughout Judah.

Did you know? In his prayer, Jehoshaphat declares that the LORD is the God of heaven and rules over all the kingdoms of the nations, and that power and might are in His hand, so that no one can stand against Him.

Did you know? Jehoshaphat honestly describes the people’s weakness in the face of the great army and says, “We do not know what to do”; nevertheless, he emphasizes that their eyes are fixed on the LORD.
Did you know? Jahaziel, who delivered the word of the LORD to the people, was a Levite descended from Asaph. According to the verse, the Spirit of the LORD came upon him in the midst of the assembly.

Did you know? The central message of the prophecy was that Judah was not required to fight the battle itself: “The battle is not yours, but God’s”; the people were commanded to take their positions and see the LORD’s deliverance.
Did you know? Jehoshaphat appointed singers to go before the army, and they went out praising the LORD with the words, “Give thanks to the LORD, for His lovingkindness endures forever.”
Did you know? After the enemies fell upon one another, Judah found so much plunder that the people spent three days gathering it and could not carry it all away.
Did you know? The place where they blessed the LORD on the fourth day was thereafter called “the Valley of Blessing”; the verse explains the name by saying that they blessed the LORD there.

Did you know? At the end of the chapter, another alliance involving Jehoshaphat is described, this time with Ahaziah king of Israel. The chapter presents this alliance as an improper act, and later the prophet Eliezer announces that the ships built for Tarshish will be wrecked.
